# Add project-specific domain reviewers

Use this skill when general engineering personas are not enough. It identifies the project's subject domain and adds local expert personas, such as accounting, clinical, geospatial or numerical-methods reviewers, with clear peer and adversary roles.

## When to use it

Use `adddomainexperts` after the repo's domain is evident from code, docs or research, and before decisions depend on specialized correctness. Do not use it to add generic enthusiasm or duplicate an existing engineering lens.

## What you need

You need evidence of the domain and the kinds of decisions that require expert judgment. If existing domain skills or agents are available, prefer wiring them in rather than rewriting their capability.

## Try it

Slash-command harnesses:

```text
/adddomainexperts Add domain review lenses for HarborTasks if its project
planning terms require specialized workflow or compliance knowledge.
```

Codex equivalent:

```text
$adddomainexperts Add domain review lenses for HarborTasks if warranted by repo evidence.
```

## What happens

The skill derives candidate expert lenses from the repository, narrows them, and updates the local persona roster. It keeps a hard seam between domain facts and software contracts: a domain expert judges whether the business meaning is right; an SDK or API contract is still established by research or a spike.

## What you get

Illustrative artifact shape:

```text
.claude/agents/<domain-expert>.md
.github/agents/<domain-expert>.agent.md
updated local persona roster files
```

The experts are local to the repository. They do not become global pack experts unless a separate pack change is approved.

## Review before continuing

Check whether each proposed expert has a concrete decision to improve and a clear veto boundary. Reject vague experts whose findings no one could act on.

## Tips and recovery

If the skill proposes too many experts, ask which decisions each one protects and delete the rest. If the domain is not yet established, run [collectknowledge](#skill-collectknowledge) first.

## Where to go next

Use the experts during [specify](#skill-specify), [define architecture](#skill-define-architecture), or [design a slice](#skill-design-slice) when domain correctness affects the outcome.
